newsitem.title: USA: Dow barrels to yet another record high.
newsitem.headline: Dow barrels to yet another record high.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average barrelled to its second straight record high close on Wednesday, moving further above the 8,000-point level after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan painted a near-perfect picture of the economy.
The blue-chip Dow index ended up 26.71 points at a new high of 8,088.36, one day after soaring 155 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,714 to 1,152 on active volume of 616 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The latest reports of strong corporate earnings growth also help propel the market higher as Greenspan concluded his two-day report to Congress on the state of the economy.

During his testimony, Greenspan repeated his rosy moderate-growth, low-inflation appraisal of the economy and reinforced analysts' impression that the Fed was unlikely to raise interest rates anytime soon.
"I think the die was cast yesterday," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "In effect, Greenspan has told us not to worry about the August or September Fed meetings."
Stocks surged early on Greenspan's comments but faded a bit when Fed Vice Chair Alice Rivlin later cautioned that it was a "close call" on whether interest rates should rise.
Rivlin's comments tempered but failed to quash Wall Street's enthusiasm, given Greenspan's upbeat assessment of the economy.
"Alan Greenspan really rules the Fed," Wachtel said.
With their interest rate worries allayed, investors were again free to focus on corporate earnings, where the trend remained positive.

Among Dow components, chemical and energy giant DuPont Co. gained 1-7/16 to 67-5/8 after reporting its income rose 14 percent from a year ago. AlliedSignal Inc., which also posted a strong earnings gain of 16 percent, rose 1-1/16 to 92-1/4.
The results highlighted another day of strong earnings and buttressed the stock market in its relentless climb into record territory.

"There's no reason to buy stocks other than to participate in the earnings growth of the companies, and the second-quarter results have generally been coming in above consensus," said Al Goldman, an analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.

The Dow index got its biggest lift from aerospace giant Boeing Co., which climbed 2-11/16 to 59-1/16 after winning European Union approval for its merger with McDonnell Douglas Co., whose stock rose 4-5/16 to 76-1/16.
Computer Associates International Inc. surged 5-1/4 to 69 9/16 after the software maker reported earnings jumped 30 percent for the quarter, beating Wall Street estimates.

There were disappointments, however. Anheuser-Busch Cos., fell 2-5/8 to 45-1/4 after it reported slightly higher second quarter earnings and said full year earnings growth would fall slightly below long-term objectives due to heavy discounting in the beer industry.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.79 points to 1,567.65.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.58 to 936.56. The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.45 to 634.65.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.62 to 485.51, a new high. The average share was up 15 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,863.615, up 29.544, or 0.33 percent.
